source: Pathak et al. (2017) Curiosity-driven Exploration by Self-supervised Prediction
finding: ICM rewards the error of a forward model in a learned feature space. It solved sparse-reward VizDoom where A3C failed.
numbers: VizDoom sparse setup, mean (median) score at convergence: ICM+A3C 100% (100%); TRPO 26.0% (0.0%); A3C 0.0%; VIME+TRPO 46.1% (27.1%). Noise-source sanity check (uniform, Gaussian, Laplacian) never reached the goal.
limits: Tiny task, one fixed layout. Authors admit the agent's own stochasticity can be exploited. Features were built to ignore uncontrollable pixels.
agent_relevance: Prediction-error bonus only works if the model can ignore noise. A text agent has no such feature space.

source: Pathak et al. (2017) ICM, noise robustness test
finding: With 40% of the screen replaced by white noise, ICM still succeeded most of the time. A pixel-prediction variant struggled.
numbers: Distractor = 40% of visual observation replaced with white noise (Fig. 6).
limits: Noise was uncontrollable and not caused by agent actions. Later work shows agent-caused noise breaks it.
agent_relevance: Ignore noise that actions cannot change; this is the basic fix for the noisy TV.

source: Burda et al. (2018) Large-Scale Study of Curiosity-Driven Learning
finding: Pure curiosity (no extrinsic reward) gave good play across 54 environments. Random features did about as well as learned ones. A literal noisy TV slows learning.
numbers: 54 environments incl. Atari suite, Mario, Unity maze. With the noisy TV added the agent learns drastically slower, but sometimes still converges if run long enough.
limits: Many Atari games reward staying alive, so curiosity aligns with score. Success is not proof of general curiosity.
agent_relevance: Curiosity can look good where the task already rewards survival and novelty. Check alignment before crediting the bonus.

source: Burda et al. (2018) Large-scale study, failure case
finding: Prediction error equals transition entropy under stochastic dynamics, so agents seek the noisiest transitions. Poor models or partial observability cause the same trap.
numbers: Noisy-TV experiment on the Unity maze comparing IDF and random-feature agents with and without TV (Fig. 6).
quote: If the transitions in the environment are random, then even with a perfect dynamics model, the expected reward will be the entropy of the transition
limits: Authors saw no such effect in the game suites, so the trap is shown only in a designed setting.
agent_relevance: A text agent that rewards itself for surprising model outputs will chase random text.

source: Burda, Edwards, Storkey, Klimov (2018) Exploration by Random Network Distillation
finding: RND uses the error of predicting a fixed random network. It removes the stochastic-target source of error. First method above average human on Montezuma's Revenge.
numbers: Without extrinsic reward the agent finds more than half the rooms. Best agent often finds 22 of 24 rooms on level 1. Mean returns 7,570 (1.6B frames) and 10,070 (RNN, 1024 envs). Pitfall!: both methods find no positive reward.
limits: Montezuma ablated heavily and tuned on it. Fails on Pitfall!.
agent_relevance: The target of the prediction must be deterministic, or the bonus measures noise, not learning.

source: Taiga et al. (2019) On Bonus-Based Exploration Methods in the Arcade Learning Environment
finding: Controlled comparison on Rainbow with 200M frames. Newer bonuses (RND, ICM) gave no significant gain on Montezuma over older methods, and epsilon-greedy and NoisyNets were competitive.
numbers: Seven hard-exploration games plus the Atari training set; 200M frames fixed. On easy games pseudo-counts did worse on every game except Seaquest; RND and ICM matched but did not exceed epsilon-greedy.
quote: bonus-based methods are generally detrimental in the context of easy exploration problems
limits: Rainbow value-based agent, not the PPO setup of the RND paper, so partly a boundary condition. Hyperparameters tuned on Montezuma only.
agent_relevance: Intrinsic bonus can hurt when exploration is easy. Gate it by need.

source: Taiga et al. (2019) Atari follow-up finding
finding: Headline gains of RND on Montezuma largely do not transfer to a different agent and sample budget. Claims depend on the training algorithm.
numbers: Same Rainbow setting; hard games show no consistent bonus advantage over epsilon-greedy.
limits: Setting differs from original (PPO, billions of frames), so this is not a pure failure.
agent_relevance: Report results by setup; do not carry a bonus method between scaffolds untested.

source: Pathak, Gandhi, Gupta (2019) Self-Supervised Exploration via Disagreement
finding: Reward = variance across an ensemble of forward models. Variance drops as models learn and stays low for pure noise, so the TV is ignored. It still fails when the agent itself causes the stochasticity.
numbers: Tested on stochastic Atari, Mujoco, Unity and a real robot; differentiable policy optimisation without RL.
limits: Paper states observation-noise methods fail when the agent is the source of stochasticity; ensemble costs more.
agent_relevance: Use disagreement between several model attempts, not error against one answer. This maps to sampled answers disagreeing.

source: Jarrett et al. (2022) Curiosity in Hindsight: Intrinsic Exploration in Stochastic Environments
finding: Learn a hindsight representation of the unpredictable part of each outcome and feed it to the predictor, so rewards reflect only predictable dynamics. BYOL-Hindsight beats BYOL-Explore under sticky actions.
numbers: Montezuma's Revenge with sticky actions: BYOL-Explore rooms visited about 25% lower and returns about 75% lower than non-sticky (authors' Q&A); BYOL-Hindsight gives state of the art there and keeps non-sticky performance.
limits: Needs structural-causal assumptions about noise; Atari and grid-world noise only.
agent_relevance: Separate noise from novelty before rewarding surprise.

source: Portelas et al. (2019) Teacher algorithms for curriculum learning of Deep RL in continuously parameterized environments
finding: Absolute learning progress with Gaussian mixtures (ALP-GMM) beat RIAC, Covar-GMM and random task sampling, and sometimes a hand-made oracle curriculum, in BipedalWalker parameter spaces.
numbers: Short walkers, final mastered fraction at 20M steps: ALP-GMM 14.9%, Covar-GMM 10.6%, RIAC 8.6% (ALP-GMM vs RIAC p<0.04). Default walkers: ALP-GMM beat Oracle (p<0.04). 12-dim Hexagon Tracks: ALP-GMM 80% vs Oracle 68% (p<0.02). All LP teachers beat Random (p<0.001).
limits: Oracle led for the first 10-20M steps. With quadrupeds even Random mastered nearly 100%, so LP gave no edge when the space is easy.
agent_relevance: LP only pays off when tasks are mostly unlearnable or uneven in difficulty.

source: Colas, Karch, Sigaud, Oudeyer (2019) CURIOUS: Intrinsically Motivated Modular Multi-Goal RL
finding: LP-based module selection focuses practice where progress happens. It recovers from a sensor perturbation faster than random module choice.
numbers: After perturbation of one of four modules, agents regain 95% of prior performance in 78k (random) vs 43k (active LP) episodes: 45% faster (p<1e-4). Also tested with growing numbers of distracting modules.
limits: Simulated robot arm; modules defined by hand.
agent_relevance: LP detects that a skill broke and refocuses practice. Useful for deciding which operator to retry.

source: Du et al. (2023) Guiding Pretraining in RL with Large Language Models (ELLM)
finding: A language model suggests goals from the scene description; the agent is rewarded for matching them. This gives common-sense novelty instead of raw prediction error.
numbers: Crafter pretraining: ELLM unlocks about 6 achievements per episode vs 9 for an oracle with the achievement tree; beats RND, APT and novelty baselines. Suggested goals: 64.9% good, 5% not allowed (13.6% context-insensitive, 16.4% not common-sense).
limits: Only text-translatable states; goals sometimes invalid; LLM prior can bias exploration.
agent_relevance: An LLM can replace the learned novelty model, but needs checking for invalid goals.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) OMNI: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness
finding: Learning progress alone is distracted by learnable but boring tasks. Filtering by an LLM judgement of interesting beats uniform sampling and LP alone in Crafter and BabyAI.
numbers: Crafter: OMNI reaches higher average task success and learns more tasks than Uniform or LP (figure only, no scalar read). GPT-3 Davinci used. Runs 33 h Crafter and 60 h BabyAI on one A10 GPU.
limits: Depends on the LLM's taste. Authors reweight their own LP baseline.
agent_relevance: LP needs a second filter for value. An LLM can supply it.

source: Gaven et al. (2025) MAGELLAN: Metacognitive predictions of learning progress guide autotelic LLM agents
finding: An LLM agent learns to predict its own competence per goal, so it estimates learning progress on a large, growing goal space. Only method without expert-defined goal groups that mastered the full space.
numbers: Abstract claim: better LP prediction efficiency and goal prioritisation; only method allowing full mastery of a large evolving goal space. Also tested on OpenR1-Math-220k competence estimation.
limits: Text-based simulated environment, online RL on a small LLM; baselines Online-ALP and expert-grouped ALP.
agent_relevance: Closest published form of learning progress for LLMs. It needs training, not a scaffold.

source: Schmidhuber (2010) Formal Theory of Creativity, Fun, and Intrinsic Motivation (1990-2010)
finding: Reward = improvement of the compressor or predictor, not its error. Boring noise and fully learned data give zero reward.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Theory; few quantified experiments. Computing progress is the hard part.
agent_relevance: Reward the drop in error, never the error. This is the core rule.

source: Oudeyer and Kaplan (2007) What is intrinsic motivation? A typology of computational approaches
finding: Splits knowledge-based motivation into prediction-based, novelty-based and learning-progress forms. Learning progress avoids both trivial and unlearnable regions.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Taxonomy; no effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Gives the vocabulary for the schema.

source: Oudeyer, Kaplan, Hafner (2007) Intrinsic motivation systems for autonomous mental development
finding: Robot Playground Experiment: a learning-progress reward moved the robot through activities from easy to hard, self-organised, avoiding unlearnable ones.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Small simulation and robot study; stage claims are qualitative.
agent_relevance: Staged order of activities came from the reward itself.

source: Kidd, Piantadosi, Aslin (2012) The Goldilocks Effect: infants allocate attention to visual sequences neither too simple nor too complex
finding: Infants looked away more from very predictable and very unpredictable sequences than from medium ones.
numbers: Recalled from memory, not opened; exact N not verified.
limits: Looking time only. A U-shape is also predicted by rival accounts such as rate-matching.
agent_relevance: Human evidence for a middle-difficulty preference.

source: Poli et al. (2020) Infants tailor their attention to maximize learning (Science Advances)
finding: Infants' attention fit a model chasing expected information gain better than models of surprise or novelty.
numbers: Recalled from memory, not opened; numbers not verified.
limits: Small sample, one task type.
agent_relevance: Supports information gain over raw surprise.

source: Bellemare et al. (2016) Unifying Count-Based Exploration and Intrinsic Motivation
finding: Pseudo-counts from a density model turn novelty into a bonus, with strong gains on Montezuma's Revenge.
numbers: Not opened; Taiga 2019 text says its early benefits became a clear detriment on easy games.
limits: Gain is setting-dependent (see b06).
agent_relevance: Count-style novelty is cheaper than learning progress.

source: Ecoffet et al. (2021) First return, then explore (Go-Explore)
finding: Remembering and returning to promising states solved hard Atari games that curiosity bonuses did not.
numbers: Not opened; details not verified.
limits: Uses restorable simulator states, which a scaffold cannot always do.
agent_relevance: An archive of states plus return is a scaffold-friendly alternative to a bonus.

source: Aubret, Matignon, Hassas (2019) A survey on intrinsic motivation in reinforcement learning
finding: Survey grouping methods into knowledge-based (prediction error, learning progress, information gain) and competence-based.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Review; claims recalled, not verified.
agent_relevance: Background for why LP is hard at inference time.

source: Kaplan and Oudeyer (2004) Maximizing learning progress: an internal reward system for development
finding: Founding paper: reward the decrease of prediction error over a short window, giving robots a self-organised path through increasingly complex activities.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Small robot demo; no comparison against rival bonuses.
agent_relevance: Defines the window-based LP later work generalises.

source: Baranes and Oudeyer (2013) Active learning of inverse models with intrinsically motivated goal exploration in robots
finding: SAGG-RIAC picks goal regions by learning progress and beats random goal sampling in high-dimensional robot tasks.
numbers: Not opened; figures not verified.
limits: Later benchmarked by Portelas 2019 (b10), where RIAC trailed ALP-GMM.
agent_relevance: Ancestor of ALP-GMM.

source: Synthesis of replication status for LP and prediction-error bonuses (from b01-b14)
finding: Evidence is strongest for LP as a curriculum selector (ALP-GMM, CURIOUS, MAGELLAN) and weakest as a general exploration bonus. Prediction-error bonuses are fragile to noise and setup changes. No test exists for LP inside a pure-prompt LLM scaffold.
numbers: 2 critiques of the bonus family (Taiga; Burda noisy TV) vs 3 positive LP-curriculum studies (Portelas; Colas; Gaven).
limits: My own synthesis; positive studies mostly come from one lab group.
agent_relevance: Use learning progress only to choose which goal to retry, and only with a competence history.
